title: Module lift for a transported ring sheaf
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(C',J')$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a common universe, and let
$L:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{Set})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{Set}):V$ be an adjunction
whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $(C,J)$ and $A$ a sheaf of
commutative rings on $(C',J')$, write $|{-}|$ for underlying sheaves of sets, and let $e_R:L(|R|)\simeq|A|$ be an
isomorphism of sheaves of sets which carries $L$ of the addition, multiplication, zero and one of $R$, composed with the
inverses of the canonical comparisons $L(|R|\times|R|)\simeq L|R|\times L|R|$ and $L(*)\simeq *$, to the addition,
multiplication, zero and one of $A$. Then there are a
functor $I_R:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ and a natural isomorphism
$e_M:|I_R(-)|\simeq L(|-|)$ such that the addition, zero, and scalar-action graphs of every $R$-module
are carried by $L$ to the corresponding graphs of $I_R$ through $e_R$ and $e_M$. Equivalently, the tuple
$(e_R,I_R,e_M)$, with ring comparison exactly the given $e_R$, is an [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] of $R$ in $A$; the construction uses the
ordinary sectionwise module operations and introduces no flatness or exactness hypothesis. The module
categories and underlying-sheaf functors are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tags 03D2 and 03D7: algebraic module structures under inverse image

proof.text: Write $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{Set})$, $\mathcal E'=\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{Set})$. Finite products of set sheaves are sectionwise products: compatible local tuples glue uniquely coordinate by coordinate, including the empty tuple. Thus their projections have the universal property of [def-weil-category-product]. For a finite list $\mathbf X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ let $P_{\mathbf X}=\prod_iX_i$ and $\lambda_{\mathbf X}:L(P_{\mathbf X})\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_iL(X_i)$ be the comparison with projections $L(\mathrm{pr}_i)$; it is invertible by the finite-limit hypothesis, including $n=0$. For arrows $f_i:Z\to X_i$, projection uniqueness gives $\lambda_{\mathbf X}L(\langle f_i\rangle)=\langle L(f_i)\rangle$. It also gives $\lambda_{\mathbf Y}L(\prod_i g_i)=(\prod_iL(g_i))\lambda_{\mathbf X}$ for $g_i:X_i\to Y_i$. These identities apply to repeated factors, diagonals, permutations and either bracketing of products, since their composites with each projection agree.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, proof; the operation and functoriality checks are written out

proof.text:
For $M\in\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ put $X=|R|$, $Y=|M|$, $N=L(Y)$. Its source operations are sheaf morphisms $a_M:Y\times Y\to Y$, $z_M:*\to Y$, $n_M:Y\to Y$ and $\mu_M:X\times Y\to Y$: restriction compatibility follows from the sectionwise linearity in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define morphisms on $N$ by
$$a_N=L(a_M)\lambda_{Y,Y}^{-1},\quad z_N=L(z_M)\lambda_{\varnothing}^{-1},\quad n_N=L(n_M),$$
and define $\mu_N:|A|\times N\to N$ by
$$\mu_N=L(\mu_M)\lambda_{X,Y}^{-1}(e_R^{-1}\times\mathrm{id}_N).$$
For the ring sort use the actual operations of $A$. By the hypothesis on $e_R$ their formulas are exactly the conjugates of $L$ of the ring operations; negation has the same property, since an additive inverse is unique.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, proof; the operation and functoriality checks are written out

proof.text:
Here is the calculation checking composite operations, rather than assuming preservation of algebraic laws. In a context $\mathbf X$ consisting of finitely many ring and module variables, let $P'_{\mathbf X}$ be the product of the corresponding copies of $|A|$ and $N$. Put $q_X=e_R^{-1}$, $q_Y=\mathrm{id}_N$, and $c_{\mathbf X}=\lambda_{\mathbf X}^{-1}\circ\prod_iq_{X_i}:P'_{\mathbf X}\xrightarrow{\sim}L(P_{\mathbf X})$. For a variable $t=\mathrm{pr}_i$, $q_{X_i}t'=L(t)c_{\mathbf X}$ by the definition of $\lambda$. If the formula holds for operands $t_i$, the pairing identity of step 1 and the formula $q_Zo'=L(o)\lambda^{-1}\prod_iq_{Z_i}$ for their operation $o$ give
$$q_Zo'(t'_1,\ldots,t'_k)=L(o)\lambda^{-1}\langle L(t_i)c_{\mathbf X}\rangle=L(o\circ\langle t_i\rangle)c_{\mathbf X}.$$
For a nullary operation the same formula follows from uniqueness of the map to the terminal object. Induction on the finite expression proves this formula for every expression needed in the module axioms. Consequently equality of two such source morphisms gives equality of the target morphisms, cancelling the isomorphism $q_Z$.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, proof; the operation and functoriality checks are written out

proof.text:
Apply that calculation to the source identities
$$(x+y)+z=x+(y+z),\quad x+y=y+x,\quad 0+x=x,\quad x+(-x)=0,$$
and
$$r(x+y)=rx+ry,\quad(r+s)x=rx+sx,\quad(rs)x=r(sx),\quad1x=x.$$
They hold as morphism equalities because on every source section they are the axioms of the sectionwise modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Their contexts are respectively $Y^3,Y^2,Y,Y,X\times Y^2,X^2\times Y,X^2\times Y,Y$; step 3 therefore proves precisely the corresponding target equalities on $N$, with the actual ring operations of $A$. On each object $U$ of $C'$ these identities make $N(U)$ an abelian group and an $A(U)$-module. The further zero and negative scalar identities follow by additive cancellation: $0x=0x+0x$, $r0=r0+r0$ and $rx+(-r)x=(r-r)x=0$. This checks all module laws without an exactness or flatness assertion about module categories.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, proof; the operation and functoriality checks are written out

proof.text:
All four operations in step 2 are morphisms of set sheaves. Naturality for an arrow $v:U'\to U$ of $C'$ consequently gives
$$(x+y)|_{U'}=x|_{U'}+y|_{U'},\quad0|_{U'}=0,\quad(-x)|_{U'}=-x|_{U'},\quad(rx)|_{U'}=r|_{U'}x|_{U'}.$$
Thus the restrictions are additive and semilinear over the restrictions of $A$. The underlying set presheaf is already the sheaf $N$, so the unique gluing of sets is also the unique gluing of the sections of this abelian presheaf. Therefore these sectionwise structures define an actual object $I_R(M)$ of $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with underlying sheaf exactly $N$.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, proof; the operation and functoriality checks are written out

proof.text:
For an $R$-linear sheaf morphism $h:M\to M'$ define $I_R(h)$ to have underlying morphism $L(|h|)$. The source equalities
$$h a_M=a_{M'}(h\times h),\quad h z_M=z_{M'},\quad h\mu_M=\mu_{M'}(\mathrm{id}_X\times h)$$
are the sectionwise additivity, zero and scalar equations of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Applying $L$ and the product naturality from step 1 gives respectively the target equalities with $a_N,z_N,\mu_N$; the factor $e_R^{-1}$ is the same for both modules and cancels on the ring coordinate. Hence $L(|h|)$ is sectionwise $A$-linear. Since $L$ preserves identities and composition, these maps and the objects in step 5 form a functor $I_R$. Take $e_M:|I_R(M)|\to L(|M|)$ to be the identity for every $M$; the definition of $I_R(h)$ makes these identities a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, proof; the operation and functoriality checks are written out

proof.text:
Finally check the generalized-section graphs of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. If $a,b,t:T\to Y$ obey $t=a_M\langle a,b\rangle$, then step 1 gives $L(t)=a_N\langle L(a),L(b)\rangle$. If $r:T\to X$, $m,t:T\to Y$ obey $t=\mu_M\langle r,m\rangle$, the definition of $\mu_N$ gives
$$L(t)=\mu_N\langle e_R L(r),L(m)\rangle.$$
If $t=z_M!_T$, then $L(t)=z_N!_{L(T)}$, because $\lambda_{\varnothing}L(!_T)=!_{L(T)}$. For the ring operations the same pairing and terminal calculations, using the given operation equations for $e_R$, give the addition, multiplication, zero and one graphs in $A$. Every displayed equation is an equality of sheaf morphisms, so it holds on every section over every target object, not only on global sections. Together with $e_M=\mathrm{id}$ these are exactly the required graph conditions. Thus $(e_R,I_R,e_M)$ is the stipulated algebraic inverse-image presentation with ring comparison exactly the supplied $e_R$.
